chapter: With Chick Webb and Ella Fitzgerald, 1936-39
title: Replacing Elmer Williams in Chick Webb's saxes
summary: Elmer Williams would not travel, and Chick had promised McRae the job; the band was house band at the Savoy.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: And I had been in town, like, just about a week. And Chick found out I was back, you know.
Elmer. Elmer didn't want to go on the road, because he always told me -- he say, "You are my next tenor player." He always kept me in mind.
He say, "Yeah, I'll keep you in mind, man. Like if anything happen -- if Elmer leave or something like that, you got his job."
I say, "Okay." You know, we used to

laugh. You know, that was the lean years when he wasn't doing so good.
You know, we used to hang out together and he was doing these gigs, and he playing at the Alhambra and Hammond Theater down there, in the (Invisible) Ballroom.
He hadn't moved in the Savoy. When he moved in the Savoy --
I think when I left, he had gotten in the Savoy. Gigging in and out of the Savoy, you know.
And when I came back, he was a house band there. He was getting ready --
He had been there all winter. That's when he had found Ella Fitzgerald -- that winter in '36.
